title_ar: الجواب الصحيح لمن بدل دين المسيح
title_es_or_en: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih (Ibn Taymiyya)
edition_note: al-Jawab al-Sahih li-man baddala din al-Masih, ed. Ali b. Hasan, Abd al-Aziz b. Ibrahim, Hamdan b. Muhammad, Dar al-Asima (Saudi Arabia), 2nd ed. 1419/1999 (per OpenITI #META# header; page markers from the Shamela-derived OpenITI text; vol. and page refer to this printed edition). Not checked against a scan.
notes: Primary text by Ibn Taymiyya; contains extensive verbatim quotation of the Christian letter (Cyprus/Paul of Antioch material) which is marked in the passages. Vol. 3 = main Trinity/hypostasis discussion; vol. 6 = miracles/signs and tawatur typology.

edition_note: al-Tadmuriyya, ed. Muhammad b. Awda al-Saawi, Maktabat al-Ubaykan (Riyadh), 6th ed. 1421/2000 (per OpenITI #META# header). Page markers from the OpenITI text; not checked against a scan.
notes: Ibn Taymiyya own text; passage T-01 reports the kalam theologians before he critiques them.

edition_note: Majmu al-Fatawa, ed. Abd al-Rahman b. Muhammad b. Qasim, Majmac al-Malik Fahd (Medina), 1416/1995 (per OpenITI #META# header; vol./page markers are of this edition). Not checked against a scan.
notes: Ibn Taymiyya own text (fatawa). Only the cited section is used; the same kalam threefold appears here at vol. 3 p. 97 (not extracted).

title_es_or_en: al-Radd ala al-Mantiqiyyin (Refutation of the Logicians)
edition_note: al-Radd ala al-Mantiqiyyin, Dar al-Maarifa (Beirut); no editor listed in OpenITI header ("-"). Page markers from the OpenITI text; not checked against a scan.
notes: Ibn Taymiyya own critique of Greek/Aristotelian logic (the "Mantiqiyyun" = logicians); the Arabic is the OpenITI Shamela-derived text.

title_es_or_en: Ismail Abdullah, "Tawhid and Trinity: A Study of Ibn Taymiyyah's al-Jawab al-Sahih", Intellectual Discourse 14(1), 2006, pp. 89-106
edition_note: Journal article, open access PDF (read in full via pdftotext).
notes: READ. English summary of al-Jawab al-Sahih vol. on Trinity; quotes IT in his own English translation (translations are Abdullah's, not checked against Arabic). Page numbers from the journal page headers.

title_es_or_en: Faris Zwirahn, "Typologies and Argumentation Tactics in Religious Polemics: An Analysis of al-Jawab al-Sahih and the Cyprus Letter", Entangled Religions 5 (2018), DOI 10.13154/er.v5.2018.44-94 (CC BY-NC-ND)
edition_note: Journal article, open access; read in full (HTML text from er.ceres.rub.de).
notes: READ. Pagination taken from inline page numbers in the HTML text (approximate, check against the PDF). Cites Roberts 1996 and Abdullah 2006 (Roberts not read directly).

title_es_or_en: Sobhi Rayan & Isa Baraijia (Abdullahoglu), "Doctrine of Fitrah in the Thought of Ibn Taymiyyah: Critical Analysis with Especial Reference to the Contemporary Authors", Journal of Islamic Thought and Civilization 16(1), Spring 2026, DOI 10.32350/jitc.161.21
edition_note: Journal article, open access PDF; read in full (pdftotext). Pagination from PDF page footers.
notes: READ. Argues IT's fitra doctrine is internally inconsistent; cites Radd and other IT texts (not checked against the Arabic).

title_es_or_en: John of Damascus, Exposition of the Orthodox Faith (De fide orthodoxa), Bk I, ch. 8 "Concerning the Holy Trinity" (Greek 8th c.), trans. in NPNF2 vol. 9 (ed. Schaff)
edition_note: English translation (NPNF2 vol. 9, Hilary of Poitiers & John of Damascus), full text read at CCEL; chapter numbering from the text; bracketed Greek footnote numbers omitted.
notes: Used as the Christian check for hypostasis/attribute claims. Not a 13th-century Arabic source; it is a Greek-language summary of the same doctrine.

edition_note: Interlinear (Greek with Strong numbers) at biblehub; the Greek word is hypostaseos (ὑποστάσεως, Strong G5287).
notes: Used to test the claim that the term hypostasis is absent from the apostolic writings. Authorship of Hebrews is anonymous; whether it counts as "words of the apostles" is itself disputed.
